assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
Time window assumed to be 1-10 September 2026, compared against 22-31 August 2026 as the baseline.
Metric assumed to be attempt success rate for UPI.

facts.text: UPI attempt success rate was 92.1% in 1-10 Sep (58,146 successes out of 63,131 attempts), compared with 93.0% in 22-31 Aug (60,069 out of 64,606).
The change is a 0.87pp fall, and the confidence intervals do not overlap (baseline 92.8%-93.2%, current 91.9%-92.3%). The change is statistically and practically significant.

Among the segments scanned, the issuer Zephyr stands out most strongly. Its success rate fell from 93.4% to 89.6%. Acquirer, region, merchant group, category and channel show much weaker concentration.
The fall in Zephyr is concentrated in the evening: hours 19, 20, 21 and 22 show significant drops, with hour 19 the worst at 11.92pp lower than baseline.
For Zephyr, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT (a technical failure) rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts (745 failures in the current window versus 53 in the baseline). Other Zephyr failure codes barely moved.

Across all UPI, UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT rose from 0.29 to 1.39 per 100 attempts (879 failures versus 189). Customer drop-off codes such as UPI_COLLECT_EXPIRED were flat to slightly lower (2.50 to 2.35 per 100 attempts).
The daily success-rate scan flagged no anomaly windows for UPI, and the data-quality scan found no issues.

response.headline: UPI success rate fell 0.87pp, from 93.0% in 22-31 Aug to 92.1% in 1-10 Sep, and the drop is concentrated in one issuer, Zephyr, where PSP timeouts jumped.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check with the PSP and Zephyr for incidents, latency or throttling in the 19:00-22:59 window since 1 Sep, and compare timeout rates by PSP route and by date to find when it started.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is concentrated in one issuer, in specific evening hours, and in a single technical failure code (UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT) that rose from 0.28 to 3.89 per 100 attempts for Zephyr, while customer and issuer-decline codes stayed flat.
hypotheses.text: A PSP-side or Zephyr-side connectivity or capacity problem in the evening hours is driving the extra timeouts and most of the overall UPI decline.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A PSP-side or Zephyr-side connectivity or capacity problem in the evening hours is driving the extra timeouts and most of the overall UPI decline.
recommendations.rationale: Timeouts are the one failure code that moved materially and they are concentrated in Zephyr in the evening.
recommendations.text: Raise the Zephyr UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT spike with the PSP and Zephyr, focusing on 19:00-22:59, and ask for incident logs.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: The daily success-rate scan flagged no anomaly windows for UPI, and the data-quality scan found no issues.
recommendations.rationale: The daily overall rate shows no anomaly window, so the problem is only visible when sliced by issuer and hour.
recommendations.text: Set up an alert on UPI_PSP_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts, by issuer and hour of day.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A PSP-side or Zephyr-side connectivity or capacity problem in the evening hours is driving the extra timeouts and most of the overall UPI decline.
recommendations.rationale: A technical timeout problem localised to one issuer and time band may be mitigable by routing.
recommendations.text: If the issue persists, evaluate routing Zephyr UPI traffic through an alternate PSP route in the affected evening hours.
